text: Why does boarding always take so long?
Back rows first sounds sensible: once they sit down, they are out of everyone’s way.
say: Back rows first... sounds sensible: once they sit down, they are, out of everyone's way.

text: But the cabin has one aisle, just wide enough for one person.
When one person stops to stow a bag, everyone behind has to wait.
They were called for the same few rows, so they crowd one spot and go one by one.
Filling every seat took a full 6 minutes 54 seconds.
What if we change the order?
Window seats first, and each person sits one row apart from the next in line.
Now six people stow bags in six different rows at once, and nobody blocks anybody.
Every seat was filled in just 3 minutes 36 seconds.
More than three minutes faster: nearly half the time.
This was a real test, run in 2012 with 72 passengers.
say: This was a real test, run in twenty twelve with 72 passengers.
asr: This was a real test, run in 2012 with 72 passengers.

text: Boarding is slow not because of crowds, but because everyone is stuck in the same stretch of aisle.
